# Overview

`im.scatter()` draws a spectral scatterplot with marginal density curves
attached to the top and right edges. Cluster identities are labelled
directly on the top density curve, following the marginal-density approach
described by Claus O. Wilke in *Fundamentals of Data Visualization*.

The function works with any number of clusters — labels, colours and shapes
are generated automatically from the classification. Cluster colours match
those used by `imageRy::im.classify()` when it plots the classification.

This document uses the four NDVI scenes bundled with `imageRy`, so it knits
without any external data downloads.

# Packages

```{r packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(imageRy)
library(terra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)
```

# The function

```{r define-function}
im.scatter <- function(
    band_x,
    band_y,
    classified,
    n_sample    = 300,
    seed_sample = 1,
    colours     = NULL,
    shapes      = NULL,
    labels      = NULL,
    title       = "Scatterplot of Classified NDVI Pixels",
    subtitle    = "300 sampled pixels with marginal cluster distributions",
    xlab        = "NDVI (winter)",
    ylab        = "NDVI (summer)",
    marginal_pt = 3 * 14
) {

  if (!terra::compareGeom(band_x, band_y,     stopOnError = FALSE) ||
      !terra::compareGeom(band_x, classified, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
    stop("band_x, band_y and classified must share the same extent, ",
         "resolution and number of pixels.")
  }

  pixel_data <- data.frame(
    X       = as.numeric(terra::values(band_x,     mat = FALSE)),
    Y       = as.numeric(terra::values(band_y,     mat = FALSE)),
    Cluster = as.numeric(terra::values(classified, mat = FALSE))
  )
  pixel_data <- pixel_data |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(X), !is.na(Y), !is.na(Cluster))

  if (nrow(pixel_data) == 0) stop("No valid pixels found.")

  # Number of clusters 
  cluster_sizes <- pixel_data |>
    dplyr::count(Cluster, sort = TRUE)

  n_clusters <- nrow(cluster_sizes)

  #  Labels: A, B, C, ... as needed 
  if (is.null(labels)) {
    labels <- LETTERS[seq_len(n_clusters)]
  }
  if (length(labels) != n_clusters) {
    stop(sprintf("Found %d clusters but %d labels supplied.",
                 n_clusters, length(labels)))
  }

  pixel_data <- pixel_data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Cluster_Label = labels[match(Cluster, cluster_sizes$Cluster)]
    )

  #  Colours: match imageRy::im.classify() default palette 
  if (is.null(colours)) {
    auto_colours <- scales::hue_pal()(n_clusters)
    colours <- stats::setNames(auto_colours, labels)
  }

  # Shapes: cycle to fit n_clusters 
  if (is.null(shapes)) {
    base_shapes <- c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8, 3, 4, 1, 2, 0)
    shapes <- stats::setNames(
      rep(base_shapes, length.out = n_clusters),
      labels
    )
  }

  set.seed(seed_sample)
  plot_data <- if (nrow(pixel_data) > n_sample) {
    dplyr::slice_sample(pixel_data, n = n_sample)
  } else {
    pixel_data
  }

  main_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = X, y = Y)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(colour = Cluster_Label, shape = Cluster_Label),
      size = 1.8, alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values  = shapes) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x        = xlab,
      y        = ylab
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position  = "none",
      plot.title       = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle    = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(
        linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey88"
      )
    )

  x_dens <- pixel_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Cluster_Label) |>
    dplyr::group_modify(~ {
      d <- stats::density(.x$X, na.rm = TRUE)
      data.frame(value = d$x, density = d$y)
    }) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  y_dens <- pixel_data |>
    dplyr::group_by(Cluster_Label) |>
    dplyr::group_modify(~ {
      d <- stats::density(.x$Y, na.rm = TRUE)
      data.frame(value = d$x, density = d$y)
    }) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # Peak positions for labels 
  x_peaks <- x_dens |>
    dplyr::group_by(Cluster_Label) |>
    dplyr::filter(density == max(density)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  y_span <- diff(range(x_dens$density, na.rm = TRUE))

  x_peaks <- x_peaks |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      label   = Cluster_Label,
      hjust   = 0.5,
      vjust   = 0,
      nudge_x = 0,
      nudge_y = y_span * 0.05
    )

  xdens <- cowplot::axis_canvas(main_plot, axis = "x") +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
      data = x_dens,
      ggplot2::aes(x = value, ymin = 0, ymax = density,
                   fill = Cluster_Label, group = Cluster_Label),
      alpha = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      data = x_dens,
      ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = density,
                   colour = Cluster_Label, group = Cluster_Label),
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = x_peaks,
      ggplot2::aes(x = value + nudge_x, y = density + nudge_y,
                   label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust,
                   colour = Cluster_Label),
      size = 11 / ggplot2::.pt, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(  values = colours, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, max(x_dens$density) * 1.25),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

  ydens <- cowplot::axis_canvas(main_plot, axis = "y", coord_flip = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
      data = y_dens,
      ggplot2::aes(x = value, ymin = 0, ymax = density,
                   fill = Cluster_Label, group = Cluster_Label),
      alpha = 0.35
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      data = y_dens,
      ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = density,
                   colour = Cluster_Label, group = Cluster_Label),
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(  values = colours, guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, max(y_dens$density) * 1.05),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip()

  p1 <- cowplot::insert_xaxis_grob(
    main_plot + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none"),
    xdens, grid::unit(marginal_pt, "pt"),
    position = "top", clip = "off"
  )
  p2 <- cowplot::insert_yaxis_grob(
    p1, ydens, grid::unit(marginal_pt, "pt"),
    position = "right", clip = "off"
  )

  cowplot::ggdraw(p2)
}
```

# NDVI data from imageRy

```{r load-ndvi}
ndvi_winter <- im.import("Sentinel2_NDVI_2020-02-21.tif")
ndvi_spring <- im.import("Sentinel2_NDVI_2020-05-21.tif")
ndvi_summer <- im.import("Sentinel2_NDVI_2020-08-01.tif")
ndvi_autumn <- im.import("Sentinel2_NDVI_2020-11-27.tif")

ndvi_stack <- c(ndvi_winter, ndvi_spring, ndvi_summer, ndvi_autumn)
names(ndvi_stack) <- c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn")
```

# Clustering the data

`imageRy::im.classify()` accepts at most three bands, so the clustering uses
winter, spring and summer NDVI. The autumn scene is loaded but does not
contribute to the cluster assignment.

```{r cluster}
ndvi_for_clustering <- c(ndvi_winter, ndvi_spring, ndvi_summer)
names(ndvi_for_clustering) <- c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer")

set.seed(42)
classified <- im.classify(
  ndvi_for_clustering,
  num_clusters = 3,
  seed = 42,
  do_plot = FALSE
)
```


```{r build-figure}
figure <- im.scatter(
  band_x     = ndvi_stack[["Winter"]],
  band_y     = ndvi_stack[["Summer"]],
  classified = classified
)
```


```{r display-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, out.width="100%"}
figure
```


```{r save-figure, eval=FALSE}
ggsave(
  "ndvi_scatterplot_marginals.png",
  plot   = figure,
  width  = 9,
  height = 7,
  dpi    = 300
)
```

# Flexibility: any number of clusters

`im.scatter()` reads the cluster count from the `classified` raster and
generates labels (`A`, `B`, `C`, …), colours and point shapes accordingly.
The same pipeline, run with `num_clusters = 6`, produces the figure below —
no changes to the function or the call site.

```{r example-six-clusters, fig.width=9, fig.height=7, out.width="100%"}
classified_6 <- im.classify(
  ndvi_for_clustering,
  num_clusters = 6,
  seed = 42,
  do_plot = FALSE
)

figure_6 <- im.scatter(
  band_x     = ndvi_stack[["Winter"]],
  band_y     = ndvi_stack[["Summer"]],
  classified = classified_6
)

figure_6
```

# Interpretation

The first figure shows the joint distribution of winter and summer NDVI for
300 sampled pixels, coloured by their cluster assignment. Clusters occupy
different regions of this space, indicating different seasonal vegetation
behaviour. Pixels along the 1:1 line show little seasonal change, while
those above or below it gain or lose vegetation between winter and summer.

The top marginal density shows how winter NDVI is distributed within each
cluster. The right marginal shows the corresponding summer NDVI
distribution. Cluster letters are placed at the peaks of the top density, so
no separate legend is needed.

**Colour consistency.** The colours used in the scatterplot, the density
ribbons and the marginal curves are generated with `scales::hue_pal()`,
which is the same palette `ggplot2` uses by default and therefore the same
palette `imageRy::im.classify()` uses when it plots the classification map.
A cluster shown in one colour on the scatterplot corresponds to the same
colour on the map, so the two figures can be read side by side without a
separate legend. Passing a custom `colours` vector to `im.scatter()`
overrides this default if a different palette is wanted.

The second figure repeats the same pipeline with `num_clusters = 6`. The
labels (`A`–`F`), colours and point shapes are generated automatically from
the classification, so the function adapts to any cluster count without
changes at the call site. With more clusters, the density curves on the top
marginal begin to overlap, but each cluster remains identifiable by its
colour.

The clusters are the result of unsupervised k-means. They are descriptive
groupings, not validated land-cover classes.
